description: Width tiers for Languages — F-10 sequence, Year 7-8 band. All standards are capability descriptors. C strand standards use task_contexts as the primary width axis. U strand standards use phenomena_contexts (Systems of language and Language and culture). At this band students move to sustaining exchanges in some unfamiliar contexts, evaluating source reliability, and selecting vocabulary deliberately for purpose.
subject: Languages

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest single task context or phenomenon that honestly satisfies the descriptor's command term. For C strand: minimum is the narrowest communicative context in which the described sustained interaction, negotiation, interpretation or creation is genuine — including some unfamiliar context conditions. For U strand: minimum is engagement with the described language feature across at least one familiar context with evidence of analytical understanding.
width_notes.typical_width: The full descriptor scope as ACARA intended, grounded in elaboration cases. For C strand: a range of task types and communicative contexts — including some unfamiliar — reflecting the descriptor's full scope. For U strand: the range of language structures, comparison contexts and cultural analysis described in the elaborations.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment directions that add new communicative contexts, cultural communities, historical or contemporary language influences, or task types. Width adds breadth of context — not difficulty of the same task. For U strand: additional phenomena, languages, historical periods or cultural communities that deepen understanding.
width_notes.elaborations: Target language (F-10 sequence) elaborations were used as the primary source. All target-language-specific vocabulary and grammar examples have been genericised. Elaborations are preserved verbatim in each standard entry as source record.

AC9LS8C01.minimum_width: Share at least one account of a past experience using sequenced language; use at least one argument-structuring expression and invite a partner's opinion during an exchange.
AC9LS8C01.typical_width: Initiate and sustain exchanges in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts — sharing accounts of significant events, using structured language to justify positions and invite opinions, adjusting register across formal and informal interactions, using open-ended questions and connectives to extend conversations, and interacting about aspects of Australian or target language community life.
wider: Participate in an interaction that shifts register mid-exchange — demonstrate real-time adjustment without prompting
Argue a position on a topic of personal relevance using at least three argument-structuring moves — assertion, reason, and acknowledgement of a counterposition
Record and review a sustained exchange — identify every instance where register was or should have been adjusted and explain the social signal that triggered each
elaborations: using appropriate register when interacting in different situations
exchanging personal information about routines and past experiences and responding to key ideas in questions
engaging in informal conversations with friends or family
developing narrative skills by exchanging accounts of significant events or milestones
initiating and extending conversations using open-ended questions and connectives
using formulaic examples to structure arguments and explain or justify a position
inviting others to give opinions, share views or make suggestions
interacting with target language community students in real or imagined contexts to convey information about Australian places, events and wildlife

AC9LS8C02.minimum_width: Conduct a transaction using at least three target language exchanges including price and a decision; give or follow at least two directional instructions using appropriate spatial language.
AC9LS8C02.typical_width: Collaborate in activities involving transaction, negotiation and problem-solving — conducting transactions, giving and following directions, expressing and negotiating preferences, combining group ideas to solve issues affecting young people, producing collaborative digital outputs for the school community, and reflecting on collaborative process.
wider: Conduct a full transaction — enquiry, negotiation, decision — in an unrehearsed scenario where the outcome is not predetermined
Lead a collaborative project from problem identification to shared output — managing task delegation, progress checking and final presentation
Produce a genuine community resource in the target language for real school use — evaluate the product's effectiveness for its intended audience
elaborations: working together to produce class reference materials to display key vocabulary and promote target language learning
working with peers to produce bilingual signs and posters to promote sustainability within the school community
planning and participating in learning experiences such as a class outing, stating preferences, negotiating and agreeing
planning and completing tasks involving directions to real or virtual locations
participating in transaction situations and the exchange of ideas and preferences
engaging in collaborative projects such as designing a class webpage or making a short video
combining group ideas to collaboratively solve issues relating to young people, contributing and listening to others' perspectives

AC9LS8C03.minimum_width: Evaluate at least one source for reliability using at least one explicit criterion; share at least one opinion about text content using appropriate agreement or disagreement language.
AC9LS8C03.typical_width: Interpret information, ideas and opinions across a range of spoken, written and multimodal texts — evaluating source reliability and accuracy, comparing data from different source types, responding to cultural nuance and humour, exchanging perspectives on imaginative text characters, responding to First Nations Australian authors' stories in the target language, and exchanging material with target language community peers.
wider: Compare the same news event covered in two different target language sources — identify where they agree, where they diverge, and explain what the divergence reveals about each source's perspective
Compare target language community and Australian expressions of humour in two texts on the same topic — identify what cultural knowledge each assumes
Produce a response to a First Nations Australian author's story in the target language — addressing both the story's content and its cultural significance
elaborations: listening to or reading about topics of interest to young people and sharing opinions or feelings
exchanging personal preferences and perspectives on characters, attitudes and events in imaginative texts
responding to different expressions of humour in texts from target language communities and comparing with Australian humour
listening to, reading or viewing First Nations Australian authors' stories in English and responding in target language
exchanging videos or blogs with a target language community class or student, comparing community and culture
accessing a range of information sources and evaluating their reliability and accuracy
listening to reports and creating an audio or text message to invite a friend to an event

AC9LS8C04.minimum_width: Identify at least one target language word with context-dependent meaning and provide two different meanings with sentence examples; compare a translation with another version and identify at least one difference.
AC9LS8C04.typical_width: Interpret and adjust language to convey meaning in familiar and some unfamiliar cultural contexts — interpreting context-dependent words and expressions, comparing translations and reflecting on decisions, creating informative cultural responses (vlogs, reviews) explaining cultural associations, and presenting information on topics of interest from multiple source types.
wider: Collect target language words with context-dependent meanings — produce a mini-guide showing each meaning with a sentence example for each context
Produce a critical review of a target language community cultural event — incorporating cultural analysis alongside personal evaluation

Create a bilingual cultural explainer for an Australian audience about a target language community event — making decisions about what requires cultural explanation for an audience with no target language background
elaborations: comparing own translation of a text with classmates, commenting on similarities and differences and possible reasons
creating informative responses to cultural representations of target language communities in Australia, explaining language or images in terms of cultural associations
interpreting short messages or communications, reflecting on challenges of transferring meaning between languages
viewing authentic material of target language speakers discussing their culture and language, then responding with personal perspectives
selecting and explaining individual words or phrases whose meaning can be affected by context
presenting information gathered from different types of texts and modes to create an overview of a topic of interest

AC9LS8C05.minimum_width: Create a text with at least three deliberate vocabulary or structural choices explained in terms of purpose; produce the text in a register consistently appropriate for its specific purpose.
AC9LS8C05.typical_width: Create and present spoken, written and multimodal informative and imaginative texts for specific purposes — selecting vocabulary, grammatical structures and conventions appropriate to text type and context. Create across varied formats: digital slideshows, event posters, travel brochures, biographical profiles, cartoons, short stories, role-plays, bilingual menus, subtitled video clips, and First Nations Country/Place travel posters.
wider: Create two versions of the same content for different purposes — explicitly contrast the vocabulary, structure and register choices made for each
Create an original short film or recorded performance in the target language — demonstrating command of spoken language, visual design and presentation conventions simultaneously
Create a biographical account for a specific audience and purpose — annotate every deliberate vocabulary or structural choice with the reason for it
elaborations: designing a digital poster or electronic brochure to advertise a social event related to lifestyles or cultural events
using digital tools to create a slideshow with audio about a planned trip to a target language community region
reporting on own and others' experiences of events
creating a print or digital poster to promote travel to a significant cultural location on a First Nations Country/Place
composing bilingual menus, recipes or programs for target language community-themed events
creating subtitles, captions or commentaries for texts that inform the school community
creating cartoons, role-plays or short stories about a past event or a dream for the future
using voice recording and digital presentation software to create, perform or record imaginative texts
preparing a biographical account of an influential figure
using up-to-date and emerging terms relating to pop culture, technology and media when creating texts

AC9LS8U01.minimum_width: Demonstrate at least two consonant pronunciation nuances correctly in spoken production; place stress correctly in at least two extended sentences.
AC9LS8U01.typical_width: Apply knowledge of spoken target language conventions to enhance fluency — distinguishing consonant nuances across vowel combinations, placing sentence stress correctly in extended utterances, recognising the double consonant rule in target language spelling, applying pronunciation to tongue twisters, and responding with adequate fluency in some unfamiliar contexts.
wider: Read aloud a complex extended text with correct sentence-level stress throughout — demonstrating that stress placement is automatic rather than word-by-word
Create and record an original spoken text (announcement, commentary, vlog segment) applying intonation, stress and rhythm deliberately for effect
Perform a tongue twister at full speed with correct stress, rhythm and pronunciation — demonstrating fluency beyond slow careful articulation
elaborations: distinguishing nuances in pronunciation of consonants according to vowel combinations
using the rhythms of the target language, including intonation, tone and stress, to increase fluency and enhance expression
recognising where to place stress in extended sentences
recognising that written target language has limited double consonant combinations
applying pronunciation rules to common tongue twisters

AC9LS8U02.minimum_width: Conjugate at least three high-frequency irregular verbs correctly in at least two different tenses; use at least one modal structure (verb + infinitive) correctly in a composition context.
AC9LS8U02.typical_width: Apply grammatical structures to compose and respond to texts — conjugating regular and irregular verbs across present, preterite and present perfect, using modal verb structures, expanded cohesive devices, varied expressions of quantity, adverbs to modify verbs and adjectives, and possession structures.
wider: Compose a narrative using all three tense forms correctly in a single piece — with a margin note explaining the tense choice for each section
Write a paragraph using at least four different cohesive devices — demonstrating range beyond the most basic connectors
Revise a simple text by adding quantity expressions and adverbial modifiers — compare the before and after versions and explain how each addition changes precision or nuance
elaborations: conjugating common regular verbs and high-frequency irregular verbs in the present, preterite and present perfect tenses
using present, past and immediate future tense verbs followed by infinitive
expanding use of cohesive devices to create compound sentences and link ideas
using adjectives to describe people and aspects of the environment
expressing quantity using a range of quantity expressions
using adverbs to modify the meaning of verbs and adjectives
indicating possession using grammatical structures appropriate to the target language

AC9LS8U03.minimum_width: Identify at least two whole-text coherence features in a target language text using metalanguage; compare at least one text-type convention across the target language and English.
AC9LS8U03.typical_width: Reflect on similarities and differences between target language and English language structures and features using metalanguage — comparing descriptive, reflective and persuasive language across text types, analysing persuasive language in advertisements, comparing whole-text coherence features, collecting cognates across systematic patterns, and identifying historical vocabulary influences including contact language borrowings.
wider: Analyse a target language and English advertisement for the same product type — annotate every persuasive feature in each and compare how each language constructs persuasion
Research historical vocabulary influences on the target language — identify a borrowing period, find examples of loanwords, and explain what the borrowing reveals about that historical contact
Create a visual etymology map tracing historical influences on target language vocabulary — with examples of each influence
elaborations: reflecting on language appropriate to different types of texts and comparing these with English
collecting examples of online and print advertisements and identifying language features used to persuade in both target language and English
understanding and comparing textual elements that provide coherence at whole-text level
comparing target language and English sentence structure
collecting cognates across categories
identifying target language words borrowed from different languages across time and through historical and social changes
understanding the conventions of several types of texts in the target language and comparing with English

AC9LS8U04.minimum_width: Explain how at least two language variation features signal identity or social relationship — not only describe that they differ; identify at least one language change that reflects changing social values.
AC9LS8U04.typical_width: Reflect on and explain how identity is shaped by language, culture, attitudes, beliefs and values — including religious and cultural connotations in naming conventions, language changes reflecting social values, body language and personal space conventions across cultures, formality levels and social relationships, co-official language identity, and the global distribution of the target language.
wider: Analyse a language reform or debate in the target language community — explain what each position reflects about cultural values and social change
Compare the use of different address forms across at least three target language communities — explain the social and relational meanings each form carries in each context

Compare the co-official language situation in one target language community with the situation of First Nations languages in Australia — identify structural similarities and differences in how each context treats minority language identity
elaborations: recognising that language and cultural practices are interconnected, for example in naming conventions and changes reflecting social values
comparing elements of communication such as body language, personal space and silence in different cultural contexts
identifying levels of formality in spoken and written texts and considering what these reveal about social relationships
examining how First Nations Australian languages have strong connections to Country/Place, and comparing with language variations across target language communities
recognising that many target language communities have co-official languages and how this is an important aspect of identity
noticing components of the target language that reflect cultural histories and influences
understanding the nature of the distribution of target language speakers across the world, including communities where the target language and cultures have important presence
examining language variation in relation to vocabulary and grammatical forms across target language communities
considering the value of the influence of target language culture on the English language and other cultures
